card.title: FARMAN F.222
card.text: When this unit deals damage to the enemy HQ, draw a card.
card.flavorText: The Farman F.222 was a French twin-engine bomber aircraft that was produced from 1935-1938 and used to some extent by both the Free French and the Vichy Regime during WWII. By the outbreak of WWII the Farman bomber was already outdated, it was slow, with poor maneuverability and only one 7,5 mm gun, but it had an extra long range which would become very useful in one of its most famous missions. On June 7, 1940, a single and unescorted French Navy Farman F.222 bomber variant, named "Jules Verne," attacked Berlin on a night raid, and this was the first aerial attack on Berlin in WWII, and in history. To avoid detection during the raid, the French bomber flew a simulated landing approach to Tempelhof airport before releasing its bombs on the Siemens factory and other targets, causing only minimal damage. The aircraft had racks for the demolition bombs but none for the incendiaries, so the crew simply opened the passenger door and tossed them out by hand. The raid triggered German air defenses, but despite that the crew managed to fly the aircraft back to safety to France, and 3 days later the raid was repeated. These raids were not widely reported, possibly due to embarrassment among German leaders, and were largely overshadowed by the imminent threat posed from the German forces that were rapidly advancing through France and the Low Countries. After the night raids on Berlin the Farman bombers were transferred to North Africa where they were mainly used in transporting roles both by the Free French and the Vichy Regime.
